title: MVC API Analyzers Deprecated, Migrate to TypedResults
description: Understand the deprecation of MVC API analyzers in .NET 10 and how to migrate to TypedResults for better compile-time safety.

data.text: MVC API analyzers were Roslyn analyzers introduced in ASP.NET Core to catch common mistakes in API controllers — such as returning untyped Ok() results, missing ProducesResponseType attributes, and using implicit object returns. They helped improve API discoverability and consistency but are now superseded by the TypedResults system.

TypedResults provide a more fundamental solution: they encode the HTTP status code and content type directly in the return type. This makes the API contract explicit at the language level, eliminating the need for analyzer-based inference. The MVC API analyzers are deprecated in .NET 10 and will be removed in a future release.

data.title: Action Required
data.text: If you rely on MVC API analyzers for API consistency, plan to migrate to TypedResults. The analyzers will continue to function in .NET 10 but may emit deprecation warnings.

The migration path involves changing return types from IActionResult to specific TypedResults types and replacing Ok(), NotFound(), BadRequest(), etc. with their TypedResults counterparts. The behavior is identical at runtime, but the compiler now validates the contract.

data.title: Before: IActionResult with analyzer-guided API
data.content: An API action returning IActionResult, relying on analyzers for documentation

data.title: After: TypedResults with compile-time safety
data.content: The same action using TypedResults for a self-documenting return type

data.text: If you are not ready to fully migrate to TypedResults, you can suppress specific analyzer warnings using #pragma or EditorConfig. However, this is a temporary measure — plan to migrate before the analyzers are removed.

data.title: Suppressing an analyzer warning temporarily
data.content: Use pragma to suppress a specific analyzer ID during migration

data.title: Migration Checklist
items: Change return types from IActionResult to TypedResults variants.
Remove [ProducesResponseType] attributes — TypedResults infer them automatically.
Update unit tests to assert on the TypedResults instance or the HTTP response.

data.title: Summary
points: MVC API analyzers are deprecated in .NET 10.
TypedResults provide a more robust, compile-time alternative.
Migration involves updating return types and removing analyzer-dependent attributes.
Suppress warnings only as a short-term bridge during migration.
data.takeaway: Migrating to TypedResults is the recommended path forward, providing stronger type safety and eliminating the dependency on analyzer-based conventions.
